issues.t: Head gasket leak and coolant loss
issues.sym: A low coolant warning, the coolant reservoir running empty, a sweet coolant smell, rising engine temperature, or coolant residue on the engine. Many owners saw it before 25,000 miles.
issues.why: The cylinder head gasket on the 1.5L turbo can start leaking coolant, sometimes into the oil. Volkswagen issued a service bulletin in 2023 on identifying head gasket leaks.
issues.next: Don't just keep topping up coolant. Have a dealer pressure-test the cooling system while the car is under warranty, and stop driving if the temperature gauge climbs.

issues.t: Engine stalls when coming to a stop (recall)
issues.sym: On all-wheel-drive models, the engine shuts off as you slow down or stop, and the car must be restarted.
issues.why: Engine control software on 2022 4Motion models could stall the engine while braking to a stop. Volkswagen recalled them twice (NHTSA 21V-615 and 22V-687).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Dealers update the engine software for free.

issues.t: Fuel pump can break and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine suddenly stalls while driving and may not restart.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel delivery pump on some 2022 models can break (NHTSA 23V-214, about 15,900 vehicles).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Dealers replace the fuel pump for free.

issues.t: Fuel line connector can leak under the hood (recall)
issues.sym: A smell of gasoline from the engine bay, or the engine stalling.
issues.why: A quick-connector on the fuel supply line under the hood can come apart and leak fuel, which is a fire risk (NHTSA 21V-651).
issues.next: If you smell fuel, don't drive the car. Check the VIN for open recalls; dealers replace the line and connector for free.

issues.sym: Clunking or knocking from the rear, or the rear wheels looking out of line. If a knuckle breaks, the car can become unstable.
issues.why: The rear wheel knuckles on some 2022 models can corrode, crack and break (NHTSA 22V-176).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Dealers inspect the knuckles and replace them for free.

issues.sym: The screen stays blank or shows no camera picture when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: A memory chip in the infotainment system can stop the camera image from showing (NHTSA 22V-514).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls; dealers update the infotainment software for free. Use your mirrors and look behind you until then.

issues.t: Hesitation or lurching when pulling away
issues.sym: A delay when you press the gas from a stop or to change lanes, followed by a sudden surge or lurch. Some owners describe bucking at low speed.
issues.why: Owners report a lag between pedal and power from the small turbo engine and transmission programming. Some cases are linked to sensor or fuel delivery faults.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check for software updates and stored codes. If it comes with warning lights, get it diagnosed promptly.

issues.t: Slow, jerky dual-clutch response on AWD models
issues.sym: On 4Motion all-wheel-drive models, the 7-speed dual-clutch gearbox hesitates when you pull away or ask for power, and can feel jerky in stop-and-go traffic.
issues.why: The dual-clutch gearbox used on AWD models before 2025 responds slowly at low speed. Volkswagen said owners thought their cars were broken and replaced it with an 8-speed automatic for 2025.
issues.next: Have the dealer check for transmission software updates. Be smooth with the gas from a stop. If it slips, grinds or shows a warning, get it inspected under warranty.

issues.t: Loss of power with EPC and check engine lights
issues.sym: The EPC and check engine lights come on, the engine goes into reduced-power (limp) mode, or it stalls at a stop and must be restarted.
issues.why: Owners report a mix of causes, including sensor faults, wiring harness problems and fuel delivery faults. Dealers often can't reproduce it.
issues.next: Note when it happens and have the codes read right away, since stored codes help the dealer find the cause. Ask about recalls and service bulletins for your VIN.

issues.t: Rear brakes wear out early and grind
issues.sym: Grinding, squealing or vibration when braking, with rear pads worn very thin by 20,000 to 30,000 miles.
issues.why: Owners report fast rear pad wear and sticking calipers. One owner cites a Volkswagen warranty extension (24 months/24,000 miles) for early rear pad wear.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected at the first grinding noise. Ask the dealer whether a warranty extension covers your car before paying.

issues.sym: A squeaking noise when you accelerate, often noticed in the first 10,000 miles.
issues.why: The cause isn't confirmed. One dealer traced it to a part behind the dash; owners suspect the drivetrain. It is the most reported 2023 Taos complaint on CarComplaints.
issues.next: Show the dealer while it's happening and ask them to document it under warranty.

issues.t: Infotainment screen goes blank or reboots
issues.sym: The center screen freezes, goes black or restarts while driving. The digital gauges may change on their own, and features like the backup camera or tire pressure monitor can drop out.
issues.why: Software faults in the MIB3 infotainment system. Volkswagen issued a programming update in 2023.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to install the latest infotainment software. If safety features stop working, report it.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking activates for no reason
issues.sym: The car brakes hard on its own with nothing in the way, or the driver-assist features drop out with warnings.
issues.why: The front radar and camera system can misread the road, especially in poor weather or when the sensors are dirty.
issues.next: Keep the front sensor and windshield area clean. If it happens again, report it to the dealer and to NHTSA.

issues.sym: The car won't start after sitting, or the 12V battery keeps going flat.
issues.why: Some modules stay awake and drain the battery while parked. Volkswagen issued bulletins in 2023 on finding excessive static current draw and on battery testing.
issues.next: Have the battery tested and the parked current draw checked. Ask about software updates for the module causing the drain.

issues.t: A/C blows warm from refrigerant leak
issues.sym: The air conditioning gradually stops blowing cold.
issues.why: Volkswagen issued several bulletins on A/C compressor leaks, refrigerant leak testing and cleaning the A/C system after a compressor failure.
issues.next: Have the A/C checked for leaks. Get it fixed while it is under warranty, before the compressor fails.

issues.sym: Fog or water droplets inside the tail light lenses.
issues.why: Volkswagen issued a service bulletin on tail light condensation for this model.
issues.next: Point it out to the dealer during the warranty; the light unit may be replaced.

issues.sym: The windshield wipers start without rain or won't turn off, even with auto wipers switched off.
issues.why: Owners report faults with the rain sensor or wiper control. The exact cause hasn't been confirmed.
issues.next: Have the dealer check the rain sensor and wiper switch and look for software updates.

issues.sym: The digital gauge cluster stays dark or freezes at startup, so the speedometer, gauges and warning lights don't show.
issues.why: A fault in the digital instrument panel on some 2025 Taos and Jetta models (NHTSA 26V-185).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Dealers update the software and replace the panel if needed, for free. Don't drive if you can't see your speed and warning lights.

issues.t: Fuel pressure sensor can pull loose in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning in normal driving. The risk is a fuel leak and fire after a rear-end crash.
issues.why: The fuel pressure sensor on the tank can be pulled out in a rear-end collision (NHTSA 26V-258, also covering 2026 models).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Dealers fit a wiring harness extension for free; parts were back-ordered at first.
